headline: Watch Order Secrets of The Clone Wars
post:
Did you know that Star Wars: The Clone Wars was originally organized by story arc rather than timeline? According to Screen Rant, this unique release schedule meant that some characters who died in earlier seasons unexpectedly returned later on. Creator George Lucas initially viewed the project as an anthology series, which allowed him to produce and air stories from different points in the prequel era out of sequence. 📺

Fortunately, a chronological viewing order helps the 134 episodes flow seamlessly without those jarring timeline jumps. The series is set across the three years between Star Wars: Episode II - Attack of the Clones and Star Wars: Episode III - Revenge of the Sith, with the final episodes even running concurrently with the movie. Will you be rewatching the series in chronological order soon?

headline: The Justice League hero with a Super Saiyan form
post:
Hey everyone! Did you know that the DC Universe actually features a transformation explicitly compared to Dragon Ball? According to Screen Rant, a specific Justice League member unlocks a power-up that looks just like a Super Saiyan. During Joshua Williamson's run on The Flash, Barry Allen faces a powered-up Captain Cold during the conclusion of the "Rogues' Reign" storyline. Furious and overwhelmed, Barry unleashes a massive torrent of Speed Force energy. His body becomes surrounded by a brilliant golden aura resembling the famous anime power-up! Pied Piper later warns that excessive use could cause him to transform into a "Super Saiyan" again, literally namedropping the iconic franchise. While Superman and other heroes have various temporary power-ups like Billy Batson's Shazam transformation, Barry's golden aura gives us a fun crossover vibe in the comics. Which DC character do you think could beat Goku?

#TheFlash #Superman #DragonBall
original_title: Only One Justice League Hero Can Go Super Saiyan, And It Isn't Superman
